atelier.theme: Editorial and calm, like a well-made print magazine. Big serif headlines carry the page; the rest steps back. Lots of white space, black as the only accent, thin rules instead of boxes. Feels considered and quietly premium.
atelier.voice: Calm, precise and understated. Short sentences, concrete nouns, no exclamation marks. Let the work speak; never oversell.
atelier.photo: natural light, quiet interiors, materials and details, few people, muted colours
do: Give one big serif headline per section room to breathe
Use thin lines (hairlines) and whitespace to separate content
Keep body text short and set in the sans
Show large, calm photography with generous margins
dont: Do not add coloured accents next to the black
Do not box content in filled cards
Do not use more than one serif size per section
Do not crowd the page with icons or badges

nordic.theme: Light, clear and trustworthy. A tight sans-serif, soft green accent and quiet pale surfaces. Feels modern, competent and easy to read, without trying to impress.
nordic.voice: Clear and friendly-professional. Explain what you do in plain words, one idea per sentence.
nordic.photo: bright daylight, clean spaces, people at work, soft natural colours
do: Use the soft surface for cards and bands, the ground for everything else
Keep one green accent for the main action
Prefer short lists and clear headings over long paragraphs
Align everything to the container grid
dont: Do not use more than one accent colour
Do not use dark sections except the footer
Do not add shadows or gradients
Do not set headings in all caps

studio.theme: Big, confident and graphic. Huge headlines, hard lines and an orange accent. Feels like a design studio: bold, opinionated and fast.
studio.voice: Confident and direct. Strong verbs, short punchy headlines, a clear opinion. Still concrete: no hype words.
studio.photo: bold compositions, strong contrast, close-ups, graphic shapes, urban settings
do: Let one headline dominate each section
Use hairline borders and a strict grid
Use the orange accent sparingly, for the main action and one highlight
Mix very large and small type for contrast
dont: Do not soften with rounded cards or pastel surfaces
Do not centre long text blocks
Do not use the accent for body text
Do not add decorative icons to every item

ambacht.theme: Warm and honest, made for craftspeople. A sturdy grotesque, a warm ground and a deep blue accent. Feels reliable, local and hands-on.
ambacht.voice: Warm, plain-spoken and practical, like the owner explaining the job. Mention the work, the materials and the region.
ambacht.photo: craftsmen at work, hands and tools, real materials, warm light, finished projects
do: Show real work and real people as much as possible
Use the warm surface for cards and the blue for actions
Put contact details and the main call to action within easy reach
Use rounded, friendly shapes for buttons
dont: Do not use cold greys or a dark theme
Do not use abstract stock imagery
Do not use thin, light fonts for headings
Do not hide the phone number

helder.theme: Trusted and accessible. Rounded shapes, soft flat surfaces and a petrol accent. Feels caring and calm, easy for everyone to use.
helder.voice: Reassuring and simple. Short sentences, no jargon, speak to the reader directly and explain the next step.
helder.photo: warm caring moments, people talking, bright welcoming spaces, soft colours
do: Keep text large enough and contrast high
Use soft surfaces to group related content
Make the next step obvious on every page
Use rounded corners consistently
dont: Do not use small or light grey text
Do not use dark or loud sections
Do not use sharp, aggressive shapes
Do not stack several calls to action next to each other

noir.theme: Dark and exclusive. A fine serif, champagne accent and large photography on a near-black ground. Feels evening, intimate and premium.
noir.voice: Refined and evocative but still precise. Few words, sensory detail, an invitation rather than a sales pitch.
noir.photo: moody low light, evening atmosphere, rich textures, close-up details, warm highlights
do: Let large photography fill the space
Use the champagne accent only for actions and fine details
Use uppercase letter-spaced labels for buttons and small headings
Keep generous spacing between sections
dont: Do not use bright colours or white sections
Do not use small grey text on the dark ground
Do not use rounded, playful shapes
Do not use bright daylight stock photos

raster.theme: Swiss and technical. White, black and a single red, everything on a strict grid with hairlines. Feels precise, engineered and no-nonsense.
raster.voice: Factual and exact. Numbers, specifications and clear claims; no adjectives that cannot be measured.
raster.photo: architectural lines, technical details, clean product shots, strong geometry
do: Put every element on the grid, aligned to columns
Use hairlines to divide content
Use the red only for the main action and key numbers
Use square corners everywhere
dont: Do not round corners or use soft shadows
Do not add a second accent colour
Do not centre text
Do not use decorative illustrations

fris.theme: Friendly and modern for local services. A rounded sans, white ground and cobalt blue. Feels approachable, quick and easy to contact.
fris.voice: Friendly, direct and helpful. Say what you do, where and how to reach you; invite the reader to call or ask a quote.
fris.photo: bright daylight, friendly people, service at home, clean modern spaces
do: Make the main action (call, quote, booking) visible in the header and hero
Use flat light cards to group services
Keep icons simple and consistent
Use rounded buttons with a clear label
dont: Do not use dark themes or heavy imagery
Do not use serif headlines
Do not use long paragraphs
Do not use more than one accent colour
